summary: Your 2001 Acura Integra has made it an incredible 316,000 miles, but it has several open recalls on the lights and airbags that need attention.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement lamps were sold without the required amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: The manufacturer will replace the lamps for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement headlights and marker lights do not have amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: The manufacturer will replace the lamps for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement corner lights and headlights lack amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: The manufacturer will offer to repurchase the lamps.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain aftermarket headlights and corner lights were sold without amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: The manufacturer will offer reimbursement for the purchase of the lights.

recalls.summary_plain: Some passenger air bag modules were not properly welded and might fail to deploy in a crash.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will replace the passenger air bag module for free.

known_problems.explanation: Drivers have reported issues with tires, which are the rubber rings that grip the road.
Drivers have reported issues with air bags, which are safety cushions that inflate during a crash.
Drivers have reported issues with the power train, which includes the engine parts that send power to the wheels.
Drivers have reported issues with the engine and engine cooling system, which keeps the motor from overheating.
Drivers have reported issues with the steering, which is the system that turns your front wheels.

maintenance_due.why: The timing belt is a rubber band that keeps internal engine parts moving together, and it wears out over time.
Spark plugs create the small fires inside your engine that make it run.
Coolant is the liquid that flows through your engine to keep it from getting too hot.
Transmission fluid is the oil that helps your car change gears smoothly.
Brake fluid is the liquid that pushes your brakes to help you stop.

declined_services.risk_if_ignored: If the timing belt snaps, your engine will experience catastrophic internal damage and stop working completely.
Old fluid can cause your transmission to fail, meaning your car will no longer be able to drive.
Old coolant can cause your engine to overheat, leading to warped engine parts and complete engine failure.
Old fluid absorbs water and can cause your brakes to feel spongy or fail completely.
Worn plugs will cause your engine to misfire, run poorly, and waste a lot of fuel.

disclaimers: Costs and difficulty are estimates, not quotes.
Brakes, airbags, and fuel lines: have a professional check your work.
